name: Eurocentrism
summary: Eurocentrism is the worldview that treats Europe or the West as the centre of world events and as superior to other cultures, presenting the European perspective as objective or universal. In its classical form it ranked peoples and civilizations in a developmental scale with Europe at the top and held that the advanced had a right, even a duty, to rule and civilise the rest.
scope: The classical nineteenth-century Eurocentric outlook of imperial Europe, as seen in Hegel's philosophy of history, Jules Ferry's 1884 case for colonial expansion, Kipling's 'White Man's Burden' and Mill-style liberal tutelage, with its modern echo in Western-centred history and knowledge. It is an analytic label more often applied by critics than adopted by adherents, and it carries no programme on welfare, taxation or social policy, so most domestic answers are low-confidence inferences.

keyFigures.name: Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel
keyFigures.role: Philosopher whose world history makes Europe the end of history and Asia its beginning.

keyFigures.name: Jules Ferry
keyFigures.role: French premier who argued that higher races have a right and duty to rule lower ones.

keyFigures.name: Rudyard Kipling
keyFigures.role: Poet whose 1899 poem presented imperial rule over non-white peoples as a moral burden.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Eurocentrism is a view of civilizational rank, not a welfare programme; adherents ranged from liberals to conservatives, so the issue is not settled by the worldview.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Nothing in the worldview addresses wage law; classical adherents split along ordinary liberal and conservative lines.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Ferry-style imperial liberalism prized commerce and open outlets for industry, and Mill's commercial society was seen as a civilizing stage, so a mild market lean is inferred.

public-ownership.rationale: Classical adherents were mostly bourgeois liberals or conservatives who backed private enterprise with state backing for empire, so nationalised industry is inferred as disfavoured.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Nineteenth-century Eurocentric elites were generally propertied and not redistributive; the worldview itself is silent, so this is inferred.

unions-good.rationale: The worldview has no stated labour position; adherents were found in both pro- and anti-union camps.

property-fundamental.rationale: Liberal-imperial thought treated secure property and commercial society as marks of advanced civilization, so a modest agree is inferred.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Imperial chartered companies were praised as agents of expansion, but adherents did not share a regulatory line; the issue is outside the worldview.

cut-welfare.rationale: No documented position; adherents split between paternalist conservatives and laissez-faire liberals.

worker-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the bourgeois, order-minded outlook of classical proponents, who did not advance worker ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed by the worldview; colonial administrations did use heavy policing, but adherents as such took no common line.

legalize-drugs.rationale: A moral-cultural question outside the worldview; adherents are split.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Adherents defended beliefs in racial and civilizational hierarchy that such laws would target, so they would oppose restrictions; inferred.

strong-leader.rationale: Imperial expansion was championed by both parliamentary statesmen like Ferry and authoritarians; no shared stance.

state-harmful.rationale: The doctrine rests on strong states ruling colonies and holding a civilizing duty; Ferry treats abstention as the road to decadence.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed by the worldview; adherents differ by country and party.

empower-police-military.rationale: Colonial expansion and rule required armed force and naval power, as Ferry's coaling-station argument shows, so adherents back military strength.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: A morals question the worldview does not decide.

decide-locally.rationale: Empire was administered from the metropole and presumed the colonised were unfit to decide for themselves; inferred as a lean to central authority.

rehabilitation.rationale: Penal philosophy is outside the worldview; adherents split.

traditional-family.rationale: Victorian-era adherents generally upheld Christian family norms as part of European civilization, though this is inferred, not defining.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Historical adherents were socially conservative, but modern Western-centric thinkers sometimes cite it as a Western value; inferred and split.

more-religion-public.rationale: Christianity was often counted among Europe's civilizing gifts, as in Spanish and later missionary arguments, so a mild agree is inferred.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Adherents held a racial hierarchy as natural or developmental, so they would not see correcting past racial injustice as a duty; Ferry asserts higher races hold rights over lower.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from the naturalising, hierarchical categories characteristic of the period; not a documented position.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Adherents prize European or Western cultural heritage as superior and worth defending, and the national frame is common in the sources.

gradual-change.rationale: Hegel's constitutional monarchy and Mill's staged tutelage both treat orderly institutional development as the route to freedom.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Adherents split: some fear dilution of European identity, others welcome assimilation of migrants into Western culture.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The concert of European powers excluded non-European states from international law as the 'European Society' concept shows; adherents trust nation-states, not equal global bodies.

free-trade.rationale: Ferry sought export outlets and open markets; liberal imperialists saw commerce as spreading civilization, but protectionism also had adherents.

nation-first.rationale: Ferry grounds expansion in French national greatness and warns that withdrawal means decadence, a strongly national-interest stance.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The civilizing mission recast conquest as a duty to better others' lives, the structure of modern liberal intervention that critics trace to it.

open-borders.rationale: Adherents see a hierarchy of civilizations and mostly would not erase borders; inferred.

limit-growth.rationale: Hegel's and Ferry's accounts of progress and expansion treat growth and industry as signs of advance.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic for the classical worldview, and modern adherents are split.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Stadial theory ranked societies by material and technical advance, with Europe in the lead, supporting faith in progress.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed by the worldview.

revolution-justified.rationale: Hegel favoured constitutional monarchy and gradual freedom, and most adherents favoured order, though colonial settlers and nationalists sometimes justified revolt.

experts-over-public.rationale: Mill proposed a specialised administrative corps and tutelage by the civilised, a pattern of rule by the qualified.

central-planning.rationale: Adherents largely backed commercial economies; inferred, with no documented stance.

socialized-markets.rationale: Inferred from the commercial-society outlook; not documented for this worldview.

land-value-tax.rationale: A fiscal technicality outside the worldview.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the property-owning elites who championed empire.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; the worldview has no welfare position.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Ferry worried about protectionist rivals and wanted colonies as markets, but free-trade and protectionist imperialists both existed.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Imperial states funded railways, ports and fleets, but adherents had no common doctrine on state economic direction.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Not a concern of the worldview.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Inferred from the commercial-society outlook that treats markets as a stage of civilization; no adherent advocates this.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Monetary institutions were not part of Ferry's or Hegel's arguments, so the worldview gives no basis to take a side.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not associated with the worldview; inferred from its liberal and conservative bases.

one-party-rule.rationale: Hegel's model is the constitutional monarchy and the Western parliamentary tradition is usually held up as Europe's political gift.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Hegel held constitutional monarchy the best vehicle of freedom, and Kipling's and Ferry's eras were largely monarchical empires.

democracy-best.rationale: Modern Western-centric thinkers hold liberal democracy as a European achievement, but classical adherents doubted it for the colonised and 'unready'.

direct-votes.rationale: Inferred from representative and constitutional institutions favoured by classical adherents.

workers-councils.rationale: Inferred from bourgeois-liberal and conservative bases of the worldview; no documented support.

right-to-secede.rationale: Ferry says France will never leave its colonies, and empire presupposes denying colonial peoples a right to separate.

natural-rulers.rationale: Ferry says higher races have a right and a duty over lower ones, an explicit claim that some peoples are fit to rule others.

political-violence-never.rationale: Conquest and colonial warfare were defended as necessary and justified, so adherents reject a blanket ban on political violence.

war-builds-character.rationale: Imperial rhetoric spoke of glory and vigour, but Eurocentrism itself is not a doctrine of war; Ferry mainly argues from economics and duty.

separate-church-state.rationale: Adherents are split between secular liberals and Christian-civilization conservatives.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Europe is typically credited with secular law and reason, though Christian conservatives disagree; split, with a lean against scriptural law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Colonial rule rested on state power and imperial armies and navies, so privatising defense contradicts the doctrine.

military-superiority.rationale: Ferry's naval and coaling-station reasoning and his warning against abstention show adherents prize armed superiority over rivals.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The worldview ranks civilizations and races but does not demand ethnic nation-states; adherents are split between multiethnic empire and ethnic nationalism.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Hegel makes the development of freedom through peoples and spirit the engine of history, not class conflict.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Inferred from a hierarchical outlook; equality of outcomes is not part of it.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: The worldview treats indigenous epistemologies and rule as inferior, and critics note colonial claims overrode indigenous sovereignty.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Adherents defend colonisation as a civilizing duty, so they reject that colonisers owe compensation.

civilizational-union.rationale: Some adherents favoured a united West or Europe, others rival nation-states, as in Ferry's national framing.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Ferry mixes self-interest with duty; adherents do not share a stance on egoism.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Ferry stresses duty as the basis of right, but liberal adherents defend individual rights too.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The stadial and progress outlook treats nature as material to be developed; inferred.

limit-population.rationale: Neither Ferry nor Hegel discusses population policy; the worldview ranks civilizations, not demographic targets.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Industrial advance is the yardstick by which Europe was ranked highest, so adherents reject this view.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Pro-progress stance inferred from stadial theory, though adherents also prized stability.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: A twenty-first-century question with no counterpart in the classical sources; the worldview does not decide it.

restore-past-order.rationale: Hegel's account is progressive, with Europe as the culmination; adherents see the present West as the peak, though some conservatives mourn decline.

direct-action.rationale: Inferred from the institutional and constitutional preferences of classical adherents.

means-match-ends.rationale: Ferry defends coercive rule as a means to civilization, contrary to means matching ends.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Stadial theory placed hunting and foraging at the lowest 'savage' stage and counted advance as progress, so adherents reject return.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Commercial society with specialisation was seen as the higher stage, so abolition is rejected.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Inferred from the commercial outlook; no documented support.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Ferry presents colonial commerce and industrial outlets as beneficial, not as exploitation, so adherents reject this.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Inferred; proletarian dictatorship is far from the constitutional ideal Hegel and others praise.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Adherents defend imperial commerce and deny that it is a cause of ruinous war, as in Ferry's case for markets.

taxation-theft.rationale: Imperial states depended on taxes and armed forces, so adherents accept taxation; inferred.

harm-principle.rationale: Mill's harm principle was explicitly withheld from 'backward' societies, leaving adherents split on its scope.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Liberal adherents stress individual rights, but Ferry and others also argued from group duties and racial rank.

conscription.rationale: Great-power imperial states typically relied on conscript armies, so adherents accept it; inferred.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Inferred; the worldview emphasises states and rule, not exit.

positive-liberty.rationale: Hegel's freedom as realised in institutions has positive-liberty features, but adherents are not agreed.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not a defining view; modern adherents sometimes complain of academia, classical ones did not.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Ferry grounds rule in higher and lower races and the Hamitic hypothesis described in the Wikipedia article assumed racial endowment, so adherents lean to inherited differences.

organic-representation.rationale: Corporatist representation by family and trade body is a separate tradition; Hegel's estates aside, the worldview does not take it up.

total-state.rationale: Adherents favoured constitutional states, not state direction of all life; inferred.

national-rebirth.rationale: Ferry's warning of decadence suggests renewal through expansion, but this is not a general doctrine.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Ferry argues that expansion is a duty and that withdrawal leads to decadence, and Kipling urged the US to take the Philippines.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Hegel's modern constitutional state replaced feudal personal loyalty, which he treated as an earlier stage.

bound-labor.rationale: Ferry criticised Spanish slavery, and bound labour is contrary to the commercial-modernity ideal; inferred.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Eurocentrism presents the European perspective as objective or absolute, and critics identify this as precisely what they attack.

universal-morality.rationale: Liberal universalism that all humans share reason is central to colonial justification, though developmental history limited its application.

single-common-good.rationale: Hegel's rational state suggests a common good, but liberal adherents accept pluralism.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is a nationalist programme; Eurocentrism concerns civilizational rank and says nothing on it.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Inferred from the commercial and hierarchical outlook.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education finance is a domestic policy dispute on which adherents divide along ordinary party lines.

economic-freedom.rationale: Commercial society was held to be a necessary civilizing stage, supporting a link between economic and political liberty.

rule-by-example.rationale: Kipling's burden and Ferry's duty stress moral example, but adherents also rely on law and force.

national-self-determination.rationale: Adherents applied it to Europeans but denied it to colonised peoples, so general agreement is withheld.

force-without-un.rationale: Anachronistic; the logic of Ferry's rejection of abstention implies willingness to act without outside approval.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The tradition counts reason as Europe's distinctive gift, but Christian adherents place faith alongside it.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Whether benefits extend to immigrants is a modern welfare question that the classical sources do not address.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Workfare is a domestic welfare dispute; the worldview has no stated view and adherents split.

class-collaboration.rationale: Adherents were national-unity liberals and conservatives who preferred cooperation to class war; inferred.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Adherents prize the European cultural canon and its museums and libraries as monuments of civilization.

dominated-front.rationale: The worldview places Western powers at the top, so a front of dominated countries against them contradicts it.

workers-nation.rationale: The national-versus-international organisation of labour is a socialist debate outside the worldview.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Inferred from the conventional gender norms of the period when the worldview flourished.

ban-interest.rationale: Commercial society and finance underlay the empires; inferred.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Colonial regimes often applied racial classification, but Ferry did not argue for segregation law, so this is a low-confidence inference.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Hegel's state is the embodiment of freedom, not an instrument of class rule.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Ferry's coal argument shows fuel as strategic; modern adherents' view is inferred.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The worldview treats European culture as the standard of civilization, so newcomers are expected to adopt it.

elite-replacement.rationale: A modern conspiracy claim that is not part of the classical worldview, though some modern Western-centric nationalists hold it.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems are not discussed in Ferry, Hegel or the Eurocentrism literature, so no position is documented.

national-mission.rationale: Ferry says superior races have a duty to civilise, and Kipling urges taking up that burden, so a mission to spread civilization is central.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Inferred from conventional gender views in the period.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Adherents were elites or defenders of established institutions; inferred.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Colonial violence was defended as part of the civilizing mission, so adherents deny that states owe legal accountability for it.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic ideas overlapped with the racial thought of the period, but this is not part of the worldview itself.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The doctrine demands an active state for empire and a civilizing duty.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Hamitic and racial hierarchies were widespread, but adherents differed on mixing.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Ferry's higher and lower races, and Kipling's 'half-devil and half-child', treat peoples as unequal in rank; adherents do not accept full equality.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Inferred; Marxist theory is far from the worldview's liberal and conservative base.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Adherents hold settlement and colonisation to be a civilizing project, not an illegitimate one.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: A uniform modern legal order is held part of European legal progress; inferred.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Missionary conversion was often welcomed in the civilizing mission, so restriction is disfavoured.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A South Asian religious demand that does not figure in the worldview.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Adherents split between secular and Christian-civilization positions.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist concept outside the worldview.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Mill defended despotic rule over the 'unready' as a stage, and colonial rule rested on no consent of the ruled.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist imperial thought wanted export outlets and markets, as in Ferry; inferred.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Ferry defends conquest and the use of force on behalf of civilization, contrary to a non-aggression principle.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Hegel's history of rising and falling peoples and Ferry's rivalry for markets and bases present struggle among nations as driving progress.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Militant-democracy doctrine is a post-1945 constitutional question; the worldview is silent and adherents differ.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Colonial rule involved arbitrary domination of the colonised, and adherents justify it, so the republican concept is not endorsed; inferred.

separated-powers.rationale: Hegel's constitutional state and the Western constitutional tradition are held up as European achievements, but modern adherents' views vary.

vanguard-party.rationale: Inferred; the doctrine is not Leninist.

priority-to-poor.rationale: A preferential-option claim is not part of the civilizing-duty doctrine, which concerns peoples rather than the domestic poor.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A British housing policy with no link to the worldview; adherents have no shared line.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strike law is an ordinary labour-policy dispute that the worldview does not settle.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Not addressed; some colonial writers used population arguments but not as a doctrine.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Adherents are split: empires were multiethnic, but modern Western-centric nationalists argue the opposite.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Inferred from the constitutional institutions classical adherents favoured.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Colonial regimes used emergency powers, but adherents did not have a doctrine on this.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Famine-time price fixing is an economic-policy detail on which the worldview takes no side.

party-controls-media.rationale: Liberal adherents defended a free press at home; inferred.

party-commands-army.rationale: Inferred from constitutional ideals of state-commanded armed forces.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalisation periods are a modern immigration detail; adherents may favour assimilation but the worldview sets no timeline.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Internal party discipline is a matter of party organisation, not of civilizational rank, so no position is inferred.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Some adherents favour European unity as a civilizational bloc while others favour nation-states.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Hegel's monarch has such a role, but constitutional adherents differ.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church government is a denominational matter; Hegel's Protestant account and Catholic adherents would differ.

clerical-rule.rationale: Europe is credited with secular reason and law and Hegel treated priestly rule as a pre-modern stage; inferred.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Adherents are nationalists who put their own state's power first, as Ferry does, so they reject working for its defeat.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Adherents prize the European artistic canon; inferred.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Term limits are a constitutional detail the sources do not address; adherents differ by country.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall is a direct-democracy device not discussed in the classical Eurocentric sources.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Imperial powers kept bases, fleets and alliances abroad, as Ferry's coaling stations show.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Inferred from the property-owning commercial outlook.

people-in-arms.rationale: Imperial powers relied on professional forces and navies, as Ferry shows; inferred.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The stadial progress model ranks commercial and urban society above agrarian, so adherents don't idealise rural life.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Reunification of nations split by outside powers is not addressed; empire-builders drew such borders themselves, so adherents have no common stance.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Adherents are often scholars of the European canon.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Eurocentrism is defined as viewing the West as superior to other cultures, so adherents reject cultural equality.

death-penalty.rationale: Capital punishment was widely accepted in the imperial era, but the worldview itself takes no stance and modern adherents differ.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: A modern curriculum dispute; the worldview offers no position and adherents divide along cultural lines.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Scientific rationalism is counted a European achievement, though Christian adherents differ.

restrict-pornography.rationale: A morals-regulation question outside the worldview, on which adherents split.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Adherents are split between civic assimilation and descent.

minority-language-support.rationale: The worldview favours European languages and assimilation; inferred.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill championed eccentricity at home yet withheld liberty from 'backward' peoples; adherents split.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Colonial and creditor powers backed repayment and commercial order, and Ferry's case rests on economic interest.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Adherents deny the colonised the status that would make that claim; Samir Amin's core-periphery critique is the opposite view.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitution-making procedure is not addressed in Hegel or Ferry, so the worldview takes no side.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Mill's tutelage and despotism as a means of improvement for the 'unready' parallels this trade-off.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The civilizing duty implies obligation toward the less advanced, but as rule not aid; adherents split.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the preference for national military power.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The method of choosing a head of state is a constitutional detail; Hegel's hereditary monarch points one way, but modern adherents vary.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central-bank design is a modern economic-policy issue; the worldview gives no basis for an answer.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Ferry says France will never leave its colonies, so adherents resist giving up claimed territory; inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The social-obligation view of property is a particular economic doctrine; classical adherents did not adopt it as part of the worldview.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A Marxist dispute about the Soviet Union that lies outside the worldview.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Faith in progress and technical advance leans against precaution; inferred.

collective-defense.rationale: Western alliances are often defended as defence of civilization; inferred.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Colonial annexations were defended as legitimate and civilizing, whatever the colonised thought.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Adherents split between secular and Christian traditions.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Hegel's monarch has this symbolic role, but views vary.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Ferry holds that colonies will never be left, implying force to keep territory.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Inferred from the unifying, assimilating stance of empire.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Hegel's constitutional monarch is a symbol, not a sacred figure.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Income-tax structure is a fiscal detail on which the worldview is silent.

character-from-environment.rationale: Racial-rank thinking assumes innate differences among peoples, so adherents reject environment as the main shaper.

space-expansion.rationale: Space settlement is anachronistic for the classical doctrine, though the expansion-as-progress theme might extend to it; no stance documented.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Hegel favoured a constitutional monarchy blending elements, but this is not defining.

leader-cult.rationale: Inferred from constitutional rather than personal rule.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody presumptions are a modern family-law question that the worldview does not address.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Maoist idea far outside the worldview.

land-redistribution.rationale: Colonial settlement and private property were central to the empire; adherents oppose seizure of estates.

refugee-return.rationale: Return of displaced people is a conflict-specific issue that the worldview does not decide.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Irredentism on grounds of shared nationality is a nationalist doctrine, not part of civilizational-superiority thought.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Europe is credited with religious freedom and secular law, so punishing apostasy is seen as backward.

women-must-cover.rationale: Compulsory veiling is a standard example in the Eurocentric contrast between a free West and a backward East.

common-currency.rationale: Currency union is a modern European-integration question; adherents differ on it.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-ethnic union across borders is a separate nationalist family, and the worldview places no stance on it.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: A Zionism-era choice between emigration and local struggle for rights is outside the worldview.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Hegel's idealist history makes spirit and ideas the driver, not modes of production.

ban-cartels.rationale: Antitrust policy is not addressed by the classical sources; adherents split between liberal and chartered-company traditions.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailout policy is a modern economic dispute with no link to the worldview.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Constitutional limits are part of the Western tradition held up as European achievement.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Imperial economic blocs existed, but Ferry argues from open outlets rather than autarky.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Binding standards in trade deals are a modern dispute that the worldview does not settle.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Hegel defended constitutional monarchy and the period's elites kept titles; inferred.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Hegel's constitutional monarchy holds the ruler within a legal order, and Western constitutionalism is held up as a European achievement; inferred.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Eurocentric historiography narrates history as Greece, Rome, Renaissance and modern Europe, which critics say persists in curricula.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Mill's tutelage argument and Ferry's civilizing duty both defend temporary rule of the 'unready' by the civilised.

patriotic-education.rationale: The classical outlook held its own civilization superior and a source of duty; teaching loyalty to the nation is inferred from Ferry's national-greatness case.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: The worldview ranks civilizations and says nothing about admissions or hiring; adherents ranged from liberals to conservatives.

public-money-creation.rationale: Money creation is outside the worldview and its adherents held varying economic views.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Hegel's stadial progress and Ferry's confidence in European expansion imply a system that endures and improves; inferred.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Ferry argued that France's imperial reach was a duty and an interest, and the worldview supports continued European influence over lands once ruled.

delink-world-market.rationale: Ferry's case rested on colonies as markets and outlets for European trade and capital, so delinking contradicts it.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Ferry presented empire as a remedy for the social question for workers at home; the Marxist labor-aristocracy thesis is inferred as rejected.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Not addressed by the worldview, and adherents split between liberal and conservative positions on association and private property.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Hegel favoured a constitutional monarchy over entrenched individual rights, while Mill-style liberals favoured protected rights; adherents split.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Ferry defended the colonial order as a civilizing duty, so inferred adherents would not void colonial settlements.

elective-rulers.rationale: Hegel favoured constitutional monarchy while Ferry sat in a republic; the worldview itself does not decide the method of choosing rulers.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred from the stadial, state-centred paternalism of Mill-style liberalism, which does not give dissenting parts a veto.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred from the European liberal-constitutional tradition the worldview treats as the standard, which allows resistance to lawless rule.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Hegel gave the monarch a central role while republican imperialists like Ferry relied on parliaments; adherents split.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred from the European Enlightenment tradition that Eurocentric writers draw on; not a defining issue.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred: the European tradition accepted farming and research use with limits on cruelty; not addressed by the worldview itself.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Kipling-style paternalism presents the privileged as owing duties to the less advanced; inferred for domestic classes.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Ferry urged active expansion and duty abroad, against abstention, so inferred opposed to withdrawal.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: A Marxist-derived critique; adherents of the classical outlook would not endorse it.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony theory is a critic framework; inferred rejection at low confidence.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The civilizing-mission argument holds that backwardness lies in the societies themselves and that colonial rule brings improvement, the opposite of dependency theory.

native-born-offices.rationale: Not addressed; the worldview is about civilizational rank, not offices.

party-own-road.rationale: Not addressed by a worldview about civilizational rank.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Tutelage arguments hold that less advanced societies should be guided by the advanced rather than develop alone.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Not a defining issue; inferred as split.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Ferry and the stadial theorists held that higher races have a right and duty to rule, which excludes indigenous rule over settlers.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Anachronistic for the nineteenth-century outlook; adherents of the modern echo are split.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed by the worldview.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred: Western-centred history tends to defend inherited national symbols.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Inferred: Eurocentrism treats European institutions as the universal standard, though Hegel and Mill thought some peoples suited to despotism.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Not addressed; adherents ranged from liberals to military men.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred from traditional European domestic assumptions; not addressed by the worldview.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred: Hegel treats family piety as an ethical basis of society; the label itself has no family programme.

office-by-exam.rationale: No stated position; the outlook carries no programme on recruitment.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Ferry sought colonial markets for French industry, but the worldview has no stated position on foreign takeovers.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred: Hegel's philosophy of history prizes the rational state over popular will, so binding delegates is unlikely.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Inferred: colonial settlement and European property regimes were treated as the advanced form of land use.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred: Ferry was a parliamentary republican who defended the colonial budget before the French legislature.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred from the 'civilising mission', which promoted the European language and culture in schooling and administration.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: No stated position; colonial settlers acquired land abroad while Europeans restricted others.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred: the outlook defended existing hierarchies and would not treat unequal outcomes as discrimination.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: No stated position; imperial powers sometimes backed proxies, but this is not part of the worldview.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from Ferry's argument that superior races have a right and a duty to intervene in less advanced countries.

corporate-influence.rationale: Eurocentrism is a view of civilizational rank with no programme on lobbying or campaign finance, so the issue is not settled by the worldview.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: The worldview is silent on this; adherents might want to guard Western institutions, but there is no stated position.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Ferry and others worried about national power and numbers, but the worldview itself has no population policy; inferred as split.

residents-only-property.rationale: A civilizational worldview carries no position on local property rules; adherents split by their wider politics.

job-guarantee.rationale: Eurocentrism has no welfare or labour programme, and adherents ranged from liberals to conservatives.

democratic-peace.rationale: Eurocentric liberals did cite spreading civilisation, but the claim that democracy makes peace is not part of the worldview; inferred as split.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Hegel treats the state as the embodiment of reason to which individuals owe obedience, a view typical of the classical outlook; inferred.

non-intervention.rationale: The classical outlook held that advanced states had a right or duty to rule and civilise others, which rejects any bar on intervention.

industrial-unions.rationale: Nothing in the worldview concerns union structure.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The outlook is about hierarchy of civilizations, not secret minority plots; some adherents held racial conspiracy views, but it is not a defining element.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Hegel treats marriage as an ethical institution of the state, so abolishing its legal status runs against the classical outlook; inferred.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The worldview has no stated position on access to government information.

local-production.rationale: Ferry's case for colonies rested on markets and raw materials in a trading empire, which sits against mainly local production; inferred.

informal-organisation.rationale: The classical outlook put authority in states and civilised elites, not small informal groups; inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Classical Eurocentrism treated international law as a European public law for civilised states, but gave no general rule on national over international law.

religious-nation.rationale: Eurocentrism combined Christian and secular strands of civilisation and does not define the nation by religion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred from the civilizational ranking of Europe over other peoples, which has the advanced setting terms for the rest; the tribute framing itself is not in the sources.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Eurocentrism is a worldview with no fiscal programme; adherents divided on regional questions.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: No programme on property ownership; adherents ranged from liberals to conservatives.

defeat-communism.rationale: Inferred from the defence of European civilization and empire; the worldview itself states no position on communism.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The worldview does not address service delivery; adherents split by ordinary politics.

religion-illusion.rationale: Hegel's account makes Christianity and European culture the culmination of freedom, so religion is not treated as a fading illusion; inferred.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Ferry's economic argument and the stadial view of Europe as the most advanced stage treat European industry as progress; inferred.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Classical Eurocentric authors did not tie women's equality to economic change; inferred from the period's norms.

socialized-care.rationale: No programme for public domestic services; inferred from the nineteenth-century outlook.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Nothing in the sources links Eurocentrism to language purism; Europe's culture is held to be universal rather than needing purification.

treaties-binding.rationale: Ferry's case for colonial expansion and the civilizing mission treats native peoples as subjects of tutelage, so such treaties would be overridable; inferred.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Eurocentrism holds the existing European nation-state order as the model; no source ties it to cooperative communities.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from the colonial settlement and civilizing mission the sources describe, which promoted European settlement in other peoples' lands.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Eurocentrism takes the European model as the standard rather than a third course; inferred.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Not a programme of the outlook; settlers and nationalists within it used such claims but it is not defined by them.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred that most holders of the outlook accept the historical record.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred from nineteenth-century European norms, under which such acts were crimes.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Mill-style liberal tutelage defended liberties for the advanced, so suppressing opposition is not central; inferred.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Hegel and others treated Christianity as the peak of religion but the outlook sets no rule on punishing blasphemy.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Ferry argued that colonial policy serves industry and markets, alongside a civilising mission.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Inferred: it treats non-European resistance as backward and would not recognise a religious duty to resist Europe.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred: it ranks religious-law polities as less developed but sets no rule on removing them.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The outlook has no position on direct participation; inferred.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its developmental ranking of peoples, which did not treat oppressions as overlapping.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the conventional European norms it defended.

assisted-dying.rationale: The outlook has no programme on this; adherents are split.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: No programme; adherents come from both left and right.

alienated-labor.rationale: Inferred: it has no notion of alienation and defends the Western economic order.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Inferred from its ranking of cultures, with the West as the standard of value.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Hegel treats the state as rational and Christian Europe as the culmination of history; no stand on divine source, so split.

social-market-economy.rationale: No programme on economic regulation; inferred.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Inferred: Ferry's case for expansion relies on naval and military force to hold colonies.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred from the developmental ladder, where advanced societies lead and others follow in stages.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Inferred: imperial Europe built its own alliances and rivalries, as in Ferry's call for national power.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The worldview has no position on dynasties; adherents ranged from monarchists to republicans, so the issue is not settled by the worldview.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Not part of the worldview; inferred from the liberal and conservative imperial establishment that held it, which favoured profit-making finance.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Classical Eurocentrism assumed that the advanced Europe led and lenders and the West set terms; inferred, with adherents unlikely to favour defiance.

property-franchise.rationale: Classical Eurocentrism carries no franchise programme; adherents ranged from liberals to conservatives, and many favoured limited franchises.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Hegel and the imperial outlook treated women and nature as subordinate to civilization's progress; inferred, so a mild disagree.

reification.rationale: Not part of the worldview; its adherents mostly defended market society, so inferred as disagreeing.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Adherents were mostly liberals and conservatives of the propertied classes who defended press freedom as it stood; inferred.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Classical liberal imperialists such as Mill stressed rule of law as a mark of European civilization; inferred, though colonial rule often used decree.

racial-franchise.rationale: Classical Eurocentrism ranked peoples in a hierarchy and justified rule by the advanced; the claim is that a racial franchise followed in colonies, but it is not stated as such, so a mild agree.

online-participation.rationale: The internet is anachronistic and the worldview has no position.

open-government-data.rationale: The worldview has no programme on government records; inferred as split.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Not part of the worldview, though Christian civilizing mission rhetoric appeared; adherents were split.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The ranking of cultures is not a boycott programme, and adherents were split; inferred as a mild disagree.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Inferred: Eurocentrism is a view of civilizational rank with no programme on decision-making institutions, and adherents ranged from elitists to liberals.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Inferred: the worldview carries no stance on religious reform; adherents ranged from Christian traditionalists to secular progressives.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The worldview carries no economic programme; adherents ranged from liberals to conservatives.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Not a policy of the worldview; adherents ranged from liberal to conservative, and the question is outside it.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Eurocentric thinkers largely treated Christian Europe as the carrier of civilization, so promoting atheism would be unwelcome; Ferry was secular but pursued civilizing mission, inferred.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The civilizing mission and imperial rule relied on police and military order; inferred from Ferry's case for order and expansion.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Classic Eurocentrism treated advanced peoples as entitled to rule others, which is hierarchical, not power-sharing; inferred.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Adherents ranged from liberals to conservatives, and the worldview does not settle who should help the poor.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed by the worldview; no determinate answer.

vote-delegation.rationale: Hegel and liberal tutelage emphasize rational constitutional authority guided by the advanced, not direct delegation; inferred.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: No programme on this; adherents split.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Eurocentric thinkers of the period largely belonged to patriarchal churches and societies; inferred from the era.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Eurocentric thinkers of the period largely held traditional patriarchal family views, though not as part of the worldview; inferred.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: The worldview centres on Europe's rule of others and says nothing on local voting; inferred as favouring the established electorate rather than extending it to foreigners.

rent-control.rationale: Eurocentrism is a view of civilizational rank with no housing programme; adherents ranged widely.

abolish-ip.rationale: No stated position on intellectual property; adherents spanned views.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Imperial-era Eurocentrism included militarist and non-militarist adherents, so youth drilling is not settled by the worldview.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Nuclear weapons postdate the classical outlook and the worldview takes no position.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Imperial Eurocentrism held that the powerful West stations its forces abroad and rules others; accepting foreign bases on a European homeland is not part of it, but the issue is inferred.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Eurocentric narratives present colonial rule as civilising, so formally recognising mass killings of colonised peoples as genocide runs against them; inferred.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The worldview has no stated view on ownership and income.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Imperial Eurocentrism defended armed conquest and the use of force in the civilising mission, so a total ban on killing is inferred as rejected.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Hegel's history traces continuous development of Spirit through civilisations, not of nations; the worldview is split on national origins.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Classical Eurocentrism assumed natural hierarchies and fixed categories, so social construction of sex is inferred as rejected; anachronistic.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from the classical worldview's traditional social assumptions; the issue is anachronistic.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Eurocentrism takes no position on honouring the national dead.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Ferry and Kipling framed empire as a civilising mission with Christian overtones, but adherents did not generally cast politics as cosmic war.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred: the outlook centres the West and the metropole, not a diaspora homeland.

culture-before-state.rationale: The outlook offers no stated order between cultural and state renewal.

god-not-male.rationale: The classical outlook assumed traditional religious language; inferred and anachronistic.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred from the traditional social order the classical outlook assumed; the issue is anachronistic.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Colonial economies were run for European interests, but this is a statement about national majorities, which the worldview does not address.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Colonial borders were drawn by European powers for their convenience and ignored peoples, so merging regions along peoples is not part of the outlook.

independent-unions.rationale: Eurocentrism is a worldview about civilizational rank with no labour programme, so the issue is inferred as split.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Inferred from the imperial-era liberal and conservative elites who held this outlook; they did not make working-class power a test of legitimacy.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The worldview carries no programme on public ownership; Ferry-era republicans and Mill-style liberals differed on it.

second-chamber.rationale: Nineteenth-century European states had both bicameral and unicameral forms and the worldview takes no side.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred: the imperial-era elites behind the outlook favoured private or national ownership, not community ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred: the outlook centres on centralised imperial nation-states ruling an empire, not municipal confederation.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from the conventional nineteenth-century European view of the male breadwinner; the worldview itself does not address wages.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Anachronistic for the classical outlook; Western-centred thinkers divide on regulatory speed.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Anachronistic and unaddressed by the worldview; Hegel and Ferry say nothing on it, so it is inferred as split.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred from the imperial states' ambition to administer and control their territories and economies.

online-anonymity.rationale: Anachronistic; the worldview takes no position on digital identity.

person-over-state.rationale: Mill-style liberals in this tradition would agree while Hegel put the state above the individual, so adherents are split.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Hegel's account of history as the unfolding of Spirit and Ferry's civilising mission both speak of moral and spiritual improvement, but this is inferred.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred from the sovereignty of the metropolitan state over its colonies and provinces in Ferry's case for empire.

gm-crops.rationale: Anachronistic; the worldview takes no side on agricultural biotechnology.

dense-cities.rationale: Anachronistic; the worldview has no view on urban form.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Classical Eurocentrism ranked peoples and civilizations, but many adherents framed this as civilization rather than organised racial interest, so they are split.

racial-pride.rationale: Hegel, Ferry and Kipling affirm the superiority of European peoples or civilization, so pride in it follows, though it was usually phrased as civilizational.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Ferry's 1884 case for colonial expansion and the civilising-mission doctrine justify wars of conquest, which defensive-only use of force would rule out.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The worldview ranks civilizations rather than defining nations by language; adherents split between ethnic and civilizational frames.

communal-electorates.rationale: Eurocentric imperialists such as Ferry favoured unitary rule over diverse populations; inferred, and no programme is documented.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Eurocentrism is a view of civilizational rank with no stated position on partition plots; adherents varied.

free-public-college.rationale: Carries no welfare or education programme; adherents ranged across the political spectrum.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Carries no environmental programme; the nineteenth-century outlook assumed mastery of nature, but adherents were mixed.

future-generations.rationale: Not addressed by the worldview; inferred as neutral.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Hegel and Kipling-era views assumed fixed gender roles and male public life; inferred, with little stated.

arms-reduction.rationale: Imperial Europe expanded armaments to hold colonies, and Ferry tied expansion to national power; inferred.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Adherents split; imperial diplomacy was often secret but Eurocentrism itself takes no stance.

capital-controls.rationale: No stated position; imperial powers moved capital abroad freely, though nationalists favoured control.

missingStatements.text: World history should be taught with Europe and the West at its centre.
missingStatements.rationale: Eurocentric historiography narrates history as Greece, Rome, Renaissance and modern Europe, which critics say persists in curricula.

missingStatements.text: More advanced societies may rightly rule less advanced ones for a time in order to bring them improvement.
missingStatements.rationale: Mill's tutelage argument and Ferry's civilizing duty both defend temporary rule of the 'unready' by the civilised.

notes: Adherents rarely self-identify as Eurocentric; the profile follows how sources document the worldview. Modern Western-centric thinkers who accept universal human equality would answer equal-moral-worth, democracy-best and the race items differently.
